contents.name: Chapter 4. Fourier coefficients in ell-1(Z) (or, f in A(T)) - Goal
contents.result: Establish the algebra structure of A(T).

contents.name: Chapter 4 - definition of A(T)
contents.result: A(T) consists of integrable functions with absolutely summable Fourier coefficients and is identified with ell-1(Z).

contents.name: Chapter 4 - uniform Fourier synthesis
contents.result: Absolute convergence gives uniform convergence and a continuous representative.

contents.name: Definition 4.1
contents.result: The A(T) norm is the ell-1 norm of the Fourier coefficients, and A(T) is Banach.

contents.name: Equation (4.2)
contents.result: Fourier coefficients of a product are the convolution of the two coefficient sequences.

contents.name: Theorem 4.2
contents.result: A(T) is an algebra under multiplication, with the stated norm estimate.

contents.name: Chapter 4 - Holder inclusion sentence
contents.result: C-alpha(T) is contained in A(T) for alpha greater than 1/2.

contents.name: Theorem 4.3
contents.result: A nonvanishing member of A(T) has reciprocal in A(T).

contents.name: 3.3.3. Functions with Absolutely Summable Fourier Coefficients
contents.result: Defines A(T^n), its norm, and the continuous representative supplied by absolute Fourier convergence.

contents.name: Theorem 3.3.16
contents.result: A Holder regularity condition above dimension one-half implies absolute summability; its n=1 specialization is alpha greater than 1/2.

contents.name: Proof of Theorem 3.3.16
contents.result: Uses dyadic frequency blocks, translation differences, and Cauchy-Schwarz.

contents.name: Exercise 3.3.1
contents.result: Constructs a continuous periodic function with Fourier coefficients tending to zero arbitrarily slowly along a subsequence.
contents.reason: This is a stronger quantitative construction than the page needs; the counterexample only records the failure of continuity to force ell-1 coefficients.

contents.name: Exercise 3.3.2
contents.result: Derives a multidimensional majorant criterion for absolute summability.
contents.reason: The assigned page is one-dimensional and its proof route is the stated Holder dyadic estimate, not the multidimensional majorant criterion.

contents.name: Exercise 3.3.3
contents.result: Lists elementary algebraic closure rules for A(T^n).
contents.reason: The required Banach-algebra theorem proves the multiplication structure used here; the exercise's additional closure catalogue would not support a planned claim.

contents.name: Exercise 3.3.4
contents.result: Compares the Lipschitz and absolutely-convergent Fourier coefficient classes.
contents.reason: It addresses a broader inclusion diagram than the selected Bernstein threshold and would create assertions not required by this A/B pair.

contents.name: Exercise 3.3.5
contents.result: If f is differentiable and f-prime is in L2(T), then f belongs to A(T).

contents.name: Exercise 3.3.6(a)
contents.result: Gives the A(T^n) product estimate.

contents.name: Exercise 3.3.6(b)
contents.result: An L2 convolution belongs to A(T^n).
contents.reason: This convolution corollary is not needed in either page's proof graph and has no authorized destination in this batch.

contents.name: Exercise 3.3.7
contents.result: Records Fourier-coefficient decay for lacunary Holder series.
contents.reason: The endpoint counterexample is carried directly by Exercise 3.3.8; this separate lacunary decay exercise would not be used by its stated route.

contents.name: Exercise 3.3.8
contents.result: States an exponential-sum estimate and uses it to exhibit a Lambda^(1/2)(T) function outside A(T), proving sharpness.

contents.name: Section 1. Fourier series on T^n - equations (1.1)-(1.8)
contents.result: Sets Fourier coefficient, derivative, and inner-product conventions on the torus.

contents.name: Section 1 - equations (1.12)-(1.24)
contents.result: Develops Fourier synthesis, orthogonality, and the Parseval/unitary extension framework.

contents.name: Proposition 1.1
contents.result: The Poisson kernels give an approximate identity on the torus.
contents.reason: This is the designated FR-2 Poisson approximate-identity result; it is a prerequisite topic, not a duplicate claim for the present Wiener-algebra page.

contents.name: Section 1 - Abel/Poisson Fourier sums
contents.result: The Poisson means have the Abel-regularized Fourier series representation.
contents.reason: This Abel/Poisson summability assertion belongs to the required FR-2 treatment and is not used as a new argument in this batch's absolute-convergence proofs.

contents.name: Proposition 1.3
contents.result: C-ell regularity with ell greater than n/2 gives absolute convergence of the Fourier series.
contents.reason: The batch uses the sharper one-dimensional Holder threshold from the two other treatments; this integer-smoothness sufficient condition is not needed as an additional claim.
